question: Why was one dolphin kick made legal at the start of each breaststroke length in 2005?
answer: Because the officials could not stop it. At the 2004 Olympics Kosuke Kitajima was accused of a hidden kick in his winning 100 m breaststroke; underwater footage suggested it, but judges on deck could not see it. The governing body legalised a single downward butterfly kick on each pull-out the following year.
move: A rule nobody can see being broken will soon be rewritten.
